html:
The Macorix were an Indigenous people of northeastern Hispaniola, in what is now the Dominican Republic, when Columbus reached the Caribbean in 1492. They lived among the Taino but spoke a different language, which Spanish writers said the Taino could not understand.

Almost nothing of their language survives beyond a few words and place names, so who they were is debated. Some scholars link them to the Ciguayo of the Samaná peninsula, others to older island peoples who lived there before the Taino. Under Spanish rule in Hispaniola, forced labour and disease destroyed them along with the Taino within a few decades. The town of San Francisco de Macorís keeps their name.
